newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr may eye small upside but momentum lost.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr may eye small upside but momentum lost.

text.p: Dollar/ mark is heading for a test of a key support level that should determine its near-term trend, technical analysts said on Tuesday.
But even the dollar's ability to pass that test with flying colors is likely to mean limited gains and more sideways trading ahead, they added.
"The key level is 1.6670 marks," said Bank of America analyst Ture Johnson.
In afternoon trading, the dollar was quoted at 1.6734/39 marks versus 1.6917/22 at the close on Monday, and at 122.44/49 yen vs 123.76/81.
Johnson said the overnight action should be key for the near-term dollar outlook.
"If we walk in tomorrow (in New York) and dollar/mark is below 1.6670, the dollar goes lower. If dollar/mark is back above 1.6720, we'll rally tomorrow," Johnson predicted.
Other analysts agree with Johnson's views, although some said their charts put the key support level slightly higher at 1.6675 marks.
Even under an upbeat scenario, the dollar/mark upside is limited, with 1.6850 likely to offer tough resistance and invite solid selling, they also said.
Johnson said dollar/mark indicated it was turning lower on March 7 when it hit "1.7210 and the momentum study moved barely above zero."

"People then said there was triple divergence and you knew the trend had changed from up to sideways," the Bank of America analyst added. "Now, the dollar would have to trade sideways for a couple of weeks and form a base to resume an upward trend."
Johnson expected dollar/Swiss and dollar/yen to signal overnight what the dollar trend will be like in coming sessions.
"Dollar/Swiss led the dollar up late last year, and dollar/yen led the dollar up in the bigger picture," Johnson noted. "They'll lead the way on the way down too."
Chartists said they were looking at supports for dollar/yen at 122.00, an intermediary level, and then at 121.25. They saw no major resistance until 123.80.
For dollar/Swiss, 1.4310 was seen as strong support, with 1.4480 a daunting resistance.
Dollar/Swiss was quoted in afternoon trading at 1.4390/00 versus a close on Monday at 1.4600/110.
